title: Shutting down when systemd inhibitor prevents it dumps the user on a black screen
line: When an app blocks shutdown, Plasma now keeps the session and shows a notification naming the app, instead of closing everything and leaving a black screen.
explanation: plasma-shutdown always closed the whole session (apps, plasmashell, KWin) and only then asked logind to power off. With a block shutdown inhibitor active, logind refused with OperationInhibited and nothing told the user, who was left on a black screen with the computer still on. The open MR plasma-workspace!7184 makes plasma-shutdown check logind's inhibitors before closing the session and, if shutdown or restart is blocked, keep the session and send a 'Cannot Shut Down'/'Cannot Restart' notification naming the apps and their reasons.

commits.message:
session: Report shutdown inhibitors before closing the session

When a block inhibitor stopped shutdown or restart, the whole session was
closed first and the power action then failed with no message. Check the
inhibitors first, keep the session running and notify which apps block it.

BUG: 519643
BUG: 523719

media.caption: Master: the session (Konsole, plasmashell, KWin) is closed first, then logind refuses PowerOff because of the inhibitor; nothing is left on screen (KWin is gone, so this is the recorded state)
With the fix: the same shutdown keeps the session and shows 'Cannot Shut Down: Fake Backup is currently blocking shutdown: Backup in progress'

review.text: This is the open MR plasma-workspace!7184 applied unchanged. It fixes the real cause: plasma-shutdown now checks logind's block inhibitors before closing the session, instead of letting PowerOff fail silently afterwards. It's large but well contained in SessionBackend and plasma-shutdown, it reuses the existing cancellogout notify event, and the rig shows the session kept and the notification naming the inhibitor, with no change when nothing inhibits. Review should continue on the MR itself.
